text: Standard separate waistband running completely horizontal around the body — no interruption, no extension beyond center front. Drafted as a simple rectangle in heights of 3.5 cm to 5.0 cm; a clean frame that lets the trousers speak first.

Extended tab waistband — one side projects 5 cm to 15 cm beyond center front and overlaps the opposite side, so closure sits away from the fly. The front waist becomes one uninterrupted line; Florentine bespoke character.
Waistcoat-back band — the rear waistband is shaped like a vest adjustment system, sculpting the seat and tightening the waist. The rear of a 1930s bespoke trouser; vintage elegance.

Elasticated insert waistband — elastic sections hidden in the side seams and rear panels give 2 cm to 8 cm of expansion. The front stays clean with some gathering at sides and rear; comfort-first modern utility.

Double waistband — two waistband layers stacked vertically for substantial combined height, a strong horizontal architecture like a cummerbund built into the trousers. Smaller waist, longer legs, sartorial power.
No-waistband trouser — the waist terminates directly at the trouser body with no separate waistband piece. Minimalist architecture with nothing interrupting the line; longer torso, cleaner front.
3.5 cm waistband height — a thin visual border that nearly disappears, like a fine pencil line around the waist. Longer torso, less waist emphasis; modern and understated.
3.8 cm waistband height — slightly more substantial than standard, adding subtle definition. Refined, contemporary tailoring.
4.0 cm waistband height — the benchmark proportion and center point of traditional tailoring; neither dominant nor hidden.
4.5 cm waistband height — the waistband becomes an intentional design feature with visual gravitas, like the stone foundation beneath a building. Smaller waist, stronger shape.

5.0 cm waistband height — the waistband commands attention, dividing torso from legs like a handcrafted leather belt built into the trousers. Dramatically smaller waist, longer legs; Florentine power dressing.

Slant front pocket with a 3.2 cm drop over a 15 cm run from the side seam — a 12° mouth, with the pocket bag rotated 18° to 25° in production and a bag depth of 23 cm. The diagonal cuts across the hip, lengthening the leg and narrowing the waist.
Quarter-top slant pocket with a 2.5 cm drop — a mouth angle of 15° to 20°, closer to horizontal. Very refined and more formal, with a controlled hip appearance.
Shallow slant pocket with a 2.0 cm drop over a 15 cm run — nearly horizontal at about 7.6°. Conservative and quiet; the pocket recedes and the waist takes the emphasis.
Aggressive slant pocket with a 5.1 cm drop over a 15 cm run — an 18.8° mouth climbing toward the waistband. Maximum movement: the longest-looking legs and narrowest-looking waist; Italian energy.

On-seam pocket set directly into the side seam — the opening starts 2 cm below the waistline and runs 16 cm vertically, with an 18 cm wide, 24 cm deep bag swung inward. Virtually invisible from the front; quiet luxury and the most elegant drape.
No front pockets — the front panel remains completely uninterrupted. The slimmest hips, flattest front and longest leg line; formal, eveningwear precision.
Jetted (besom) front pocket — a narrow 14 cm to 16 cm slit set level at 0°, the pocket bag hidden beneath. One precise incision in the cloth; architectural minimalism, cleaner front, more formal.
Welt front pocket — the opening framed by a welt strip, more dimensional than a jetted cut with more visible craftsmanship. The pocket becomes an intentional bespoke detail.
2.0 cm slant pocket outlined with contrast fabric — the stripe makes the near-horizontal mouth a visible, sport-influenced detail.
2.5 cm slant pocket with a contrast stripe along the mouth — slightly more dynamic, balancing formal and casual aesthetics.
3.2 cm slant pocket with a contrast stripe — the classic tailoring angle with a highlighted opening; the most versatile contrast pocket.
5.1 cm slant pocket with a bold contrast stripe — the aggressive diagonal becomes a design statement; longest legs, strongest V-shape.
Jeans-style front pocket with a sharp 90° corner transition — utility-oriented, masculine, structured; carpenter's-apron strength at the hip.
Jeans-style front pocket with one continuous large radius — soft and relaxed, removing rigidity from the hip; casual sophistication.
Jeans-style arc pocket — a long sweeping curved opening traveling like a wave down the hip; fluid, elegant, longer-legged.
Jeans-style diamond pocket with angular transition zones — technical, modern, engineered; a sharper, more structured lower body.
No watch pocket — nothing interrupts the front pocket opening; the cleanest possible front.
Watch pocket nested inside the right front pocket, 6 cm to 8 cm wide — the classic heritage utility detail, a hidden compartment inside the waistband.
Miniature welt watch pocket on the right — a luxury framed opening; a subtle bespoke signal.
Besom watch pocket on the right — a tiny formal double-jetted opening; tailored rather than casual.
Watch pocket on the left — a rare placement that reads immediately custom, with deliberate visual asymmetry.
Besom watch pocket on the left — formal jetted construction on the uncommon side; distinctively custom-made.
Watch pockets on both sides — twin utility chambers mounted inside the waistband in balanced symmetry.
Watch pocket with a diamond-point flap — an extremely decorative, miniature jacket-pocket detail that draws the eye to the waistline.
Shallow 20 cm pocket bag — the bag stays high for less bulk at the thigh; a cleaner front and slimmer hip appearance.
Standard 23 cm pocket bag — balanced, neutral, and the most versatile depth.
Deep 26 cm pocket bag reaching into the thigh — more storage and a fuller, slightly softer drape; a longer internal hammock suspended within the trouser.
No visible pocket topstitching — the pocket appears to emerge from the cloth with stitches nearly invisible; quiet luxury.
Hairline 0.15 cm machine edge stitch along the pocket mouth — visible only up close; subtle craftsmanship.
Visible 0.6 cm topstitch border tracing the pocket — the mouth becomes a design element; sport tailoring.
Double topstitching — parallel rows at 0.1 cm and 0.7 cm following the pocket edge like twin guardrails; heavy visual structure.
Hand-pick stitching at 0.15 cm — tiny handmade dots along the pocket mouth; bespoke refinement.
Hand-pick stitching set 0.6 cm from the edge — visible artisan detailing, a trail of hand-set pearls tracing the opening.

Standard curtain lining — a floating cotton curtain (silesia, herringbone or pocketing cloth) hanging 8 cm to 12 cm below the waistband, attached only at the top so it floats. The waistband stays stable without stiffness; classic bespoke.

Pleated curtain lining — the curtain's fullness folded into engineered pleats giving 0.5 cm to 2 cm of hidden expansion when sitting. An accordion built into the waistband; bespoke technical tailoring.
Appointed waistband fabric — no curtain; the interior waistband is the selected cloth itself. Ultra clean, flat and modern with less bulk.
Curtain lining plus a Snugtex shirt-grip strip 1 cm to 2 cm wide running the waistband — a visible textured band that prevents shirt migration; executive performance tailoring.
Snugtex grip strip plus an interior retention button anchoring the inner waistband — increased shirt security and higher waistband stability.
Dedicated gripper strip — a continuous rubber, silicone or textured woven band around the interior waist for maximum shirt retention; functional luxury.
Decorative piping along the waistband edge with Snugtex beneath — a framed border like the interior of a handcrafted leather briefcase; elegance combined with utility.
Appointed lining — selected lining cloth replaces the standard waistband interior for a personalized reveal, dramatic or subtle; custom luxury.

Pleated curtain plus Snugtex grip strip plus retention button — the most technically sophisticated standard interior; outstanding comfort, shirt retention and waistband longevity, like the movement inside a Swiss watch.
Pleated curtain with multiple individual griplet zones instead of one continuous strip — flexibility while maintaining grip; advanced bespoke construction.
Appointed finished waistband — the entire interior presented as a finished design element with decorative edges and luxury materials, as refined inside as outside; showpiece tailoring.
Plain hem — folded 5.0 cm internally and blind stitched, with 0 cm of visible external cuff. The leg falls uninterrupted into the shoe; longer, slimmer, modern.
3.2 cm turn-up cuff — a subtle external fold adding slight visual weight while keeping a clean silhouette; quiet Italian refinement.
3.8 cm turn-up cuff — clearly visible but not dominant, often considered the most balanced cuff size. The leg ends with authority, not drama.
Traditional 4.4 cm turn-up cuff — 8.8 cm of fabric plus 1 cm allowance folded inside the leg. Adds mass at the ankle so the trouser hangs straighter; Savile Row bespoke.
Large 5.1 cm turn-up cuff — a 10.2 cm fabric reserve plus allowance. An unmistakable visual anchor at the ankle, the stone base of a grand column; English power tailoring.
Single forward pleat, 2.5 cm deep, opening toward the fly — 5 cm of hidden fabric volume folded toward center front.
Double forward pleats, each 2.5 cm deep — 10 cm of hidden fabric volume; upper-thigh circumference effectively increases 4 cm to 8 cm.
Single reverse pleat, 2.5 cm deep, opening toward the pocket with its center 4 cm to 6 cm from the pocket edge — 5 cm of hidden fabric moving expansion toward the hip for a smoother fly.
Double reverse pleats opening toward the pocket — two fabric reservoirs of 10 cm total hidden volume working like bellows in stride; classic Neapolitan geometry.
Single back dart per side — 2 cm intake, 11 cm to 14 cm long, removing a 12 cm² triangle to curve the seat.
Double back darts per side — 2 cm intake each for 4 cm total suppression; the waist reduces 4 cm while the hip stays unchanged, creating pronounced seat curvature.
Pointed waistband extension — a sharp nose angled 20° to 35° on a 5 cm to 15 cm tab.
Curved waistband extension — a radius sweep of 3 cm to 6 cm whose curve meets the waistband edge at 0° for a perfectly smooth closure.
7 cm waistband extension — the tab carries the waistband a hand's width past the fly for a clean bespoke closure.
13 cm waistband extension — a long Florentine tab crossing deep past center front; maximum sartorial presence.
Straight leg — hem width equals knee width or reduces less than 2 cm (22 cm knee to 21 cm to 22 cm hem). Nearly parallel seams.
Tapered leg — a 3 cm to 5 cm reduction from knee to hem (23 cm knee to 19 cm hem).
Slim leg — a 5 cm to 7 cm knee-to-hem reduction (22 cm knee to 15 cm to 17 cm hem); aggressive convergence.

Wide leg — the hem approaches the thigh ratio (34 cm thigh, 24 cm to 28 cm hem) with minimal taper; side seam and inseam run nearly parallel, the characteristic draping column of Florentine and Neapolitan trousers.
Metal side adjusters on both sides, placed 7 cm to 10 cm behind the side seams — beltless waist control; immediately custom-made.
No belt loops — a clean, uninterrupted waistband worn with side adjusters or braces; the Florentine bespoke standard.
